paragraph: [INE launched the Census 2024 Portal and the INE Angola app on 2 July 2026 in Uíge](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/ine-lanca-portal-do-censo-2024-e-aplicacao-movel/>). Its head said INE's own staff built them. In the last twelve months that launch is the only dated event found for Angola. [The tax authority AGT is building its own AI risk-analysis system](<https://correiokianda.info/inteligencia-artificial-coloca-incumpridores-sob-analise-reforcada-da-agt/>), tested since 2024 and not stated to be live. No source found since November 2023 names a third system that government staff built, run or maintain with no contractor named. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

No stage is set. [SETIC, the government ICT secretariat, lists software development and hosting for public institutions among its services](<https://setic.gov.bi/?pages%2F10253095=>). No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run, maintain or built one of its systems. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

The national agency ASIN [developed the electronic signature, encryption and secure messaging tools issued to 300 police officers in mid-2026](<https://www.dgpr.bj/techniques-de-protection-des-informations-sensibles-de-letat-lagence-des-systemes-dinformation-et-du-numerique-asin-et-direction-des-systemes-dinformation-et-de/>). [Dassa-Zoumè town hall's information systems directorate developed the Progicom municipal software](<https://www.lanation.bj/decentralisation/numerique-dans-les-mairies-lancb-mise-sur-la-mutualisation>). None of these sources names a contractor. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, ASIN [gave the private integrator MAPCOM a two-year contract to maintain the state data centre](<https://lamarina.bj/2026/08/24/souverainete-tech-comment-la-sbin-sest-fait-evincer-dun-contrat-cle-de-lasin/>). [The Justice Ministry's own information systems directorate led the instant criminal-record service](<https://www.linfodrome.com/international/127167-benin-wadagni-concretise-sa-promesse-le-casier-judiciaire-instantane-a-1-900-fcfa>), live on service-public.bj from 1 November 2026, and no contractor is named.

On 3 April 2026 the Treasury launched Lanaya and e-BDT in Ouagadougou, and its director general [said its own administration developed them](<https://www.sidwaya.info/tresor-public-lanaya-et-e-bdt-pour-simplifier-les-demarches-administratives/>). The state ICT agency ANPTIC lists [Toumnana (SIGED) and SIGEPE among the government systems it has developed](<https://anptic.gov.bf/nos-realisations/>). On 2 April 2024 the digital ministry [launched the ATI platform, developed in-house by its own directorates](<https://gouvernement.gov.bf/actualites/dematerialisation-des-procedures-de-ladministration-la-plateforme-ati-lancee-officiellement/>). None of these sources names a contractor. In the last twelve months, on 3 September 2026, ANPTIC also [helped design the ANAGRASC claims-registration platform](<https://burkina24.com/2026/09/03/burkina-faso-lancement-dune-plateforme-pour-le-recensement-du-passif-de-trois-societes-immobilieres/>).

[The Botswana Examinations Council's 2024/25 annual report says DataSmart, which the Council built in-house, was developed and deployed that year](<https://www.bec.co.bw/images/2025/annual-report/bec-annual-report-2025-final-09-12-25_.pdf>). It captures marks for the PSLE, JCE and BGCSE. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Council's other systems, Malepa, e-marking and e-authoring, are not said to be built in-house. No source found since November 2023 names three systems that government staff built, run or maintain with no contractor named. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

In September 2026 Expertise France [advertised for local IT experts to run the tax directorate's servers and administer SIGICA](<https://expertise-france.gestmax.fr/i5pour100/16150/1/safe-rca-expert-e-local-e-en-informatique-h-f>), the tax system. The posts belong to SAFE, an EU-funded project for the finance ministry. In the last twelve months this is the one dated fact found, and it shows project-hired experts running the servers. No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run or maintain any of its systems. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

In July 2026 Ivoirexpress said the state company SNDI [built SIGFIP for public finance, SIGOMAP, and the CEPICI one-stop shop for business formalities](<https://ivoirexpress.ci/2026/07/28/digitalisation-des-services-publics-en-cote-divoire-les-applications-metiers-developpees-par-la-sndi/>). No contractor is named for any of them. In the last twelve months SIGOMAP also [replaced SIGMAP for ministries' public procurement in 2026](<https://ivoirexpress.ci/2026/07/28/digitalisation-des-services-publics-en-cote-divoire-les-applications-metiers-developpees-par-la-sndi/>). On 25 July 2024 the state company GUCE CI launched [GUCE Mobile, a five-module app built and run entirely by its own teams](<https://www.gucecotedivoire.ci/innovation-et-dematerialisation-dans-lecosysteme-du-commerce-exterieur-guce-ci-lance-sa-nouvelle-application-guce-mobile-tant-attendue-par-les-operateurs-economiques-les-acteurs-majeurs-e/>). In September 2026 an SNDI representative said [it has run its own satellite network since 2006](<https://afriksoir.net/aspex-2026-le-satellite-au-coeur-des-enjeux-de-connectivite-et-de-resilience-numerique-en-cote-divoire/>).

In May 2026 a webinar record said [the health ministry's IT unit and the universal health coverage cell govern and administer the CSU openIMIS platform](<https://openimis.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OP/pages/5154603013/Webinaire+Souverainet+Appropriation+des+syst+mes+de+sant+num+riques>). The ministry handles day-to-day operations. Advanced work still needs outside support. In the last twelve months that record is the one dated fact found. It does not say the ministry built the platform. No source found from 2023 or later says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

In August 2024 the French Treasury's sheet on Congo's digital sector said [the tax system E-TAX was built in-house](<https://www.tresor.economie.gouv.fr/Pays/CG/le-secteur-du-numerique>) by the finance ministry's information systems directorate. On 22 July 2025 the ministry [installed 18 heads and assistants in that directorate](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/direction-des-syst%C3%A8mes-d%E2%80%99information-dsi-du-minist%C3%A8re-des-finances>) to lead systems including SIGFIP, SIPAE, SYSPACE and SFEC. The digital economy agency Aden [ensures the technical management of the government portal, Les Dépêches de Brazzaville said in December 2024](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/numerique-laden-examine-ses-documents-cadres-161959>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a system built by government staff went live since November 2023. Operating would need a system built by government staff, not a contractor, to go live in the last three years.

In May 2026 the head of information systems at the health insurer AMG said [its openIMIS system still depends heavily on external developers](<https://openimis.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OP/pages/5154603013/Webinaire+Souverainet+Appropriation+des+syst+mes+de+sant+num+riques>). Only two local developers had been trained, and the local firm ETECH was not operating. In the last twelve months this is the one dated fact found. No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run or maintain any of its systems. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

NOSi's team [developed the SIPP criminal-case part of the Justice Information System](<https://www.governo.cv/nosi-faz-entrega-formal-do-sistema-de-informacao-da-justica-ao-ministerio-da-justica/>), formally handed over in March 2026 and in use in every comarca. [In October 2024 the finance ministry's technology team worked to restore the SIGOF finance system](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/pais/2024/10/11/instabilidade-no-sigof-pode-causar-atrasos-nos-pagamentos-do-estado/93685>). NOSi [develops and maintains IGRPWeb and SNIAC among its e-government solutions](<https://www.caboverdeexpert.com/cabo-verde-digital-operational-nucleus-for-the-information-society-nosi/>). In the last twelve months, in May 2026, NOSi [ran the election-results system and portal eleicoes.cv with its own staff](<https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/05/27/legislativas-2026-nosi-diz-que-relatorio-preliminar-aponta-para-causas-de-ordem-tecnica/>). It also [ran the site that published the legislative election results](<https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/05/18/legislativas-2026-presidente-do-nosi-pede-desculpas-por-alegado-ciber-ataque-durante-a-divulgacao-dos-resultados-das-eleicoes/>).

On 14 January 2025 the Council of Ministers [approved the 2025 budget of ANSIE, the state information systems agency, of 556.7 million FDJ](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2025-01-14>). [ANSIE is itself building a third version of the E-JO platform](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2025-01-14>), and the budget also pays for the E-BALO platform and other work for administrations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The E-BALO platform was due to launch in 2025. No source found says a system built by government staff went live since November 2023. Operating would need a system built by government staff, not a contractor, to go live in the last three years.

On 5 July 2026 the digitisation commission HCN [launched Dzair Digital Services](<https://www.algerie360.com/dzair-digital-services-documents-en-ligne/>). It groups the online services of several ministries, and [the HCN's own services built the checker for documents issued on it](<https://www.elmoudjahid.dz/fr/info-en-continu/portail-national-des-services-numeriques-le-hcn-va-assurer-des-formations-33381>). In March 2025 the Interior Ministry [launched a police-services platform built by the national police's own engineers](<https://www.lactualgerie.com/divers/lancement-dune-plateforme-numerique-pour-les-services-de-police/>). In the last twelve months, [on 11 January 2026 the state property directorate extended Amlak to all its cadastre and land offices](<https://algeriezoom.com/algerie-vers-le-livret-foncier-electronique-avec-amlak/>). Its own staff built Amlak in a year. On 25 July 2026 [the health minister launched the national rollout of the electronic medical record](<https://interlignes.dz/sante-lancement-du-deploiement-du-dossier-medical-electronique-a-travers-les-69-wilayas/>). He said the ministry's own engineers designed and built it.

In April 2026 NOSI said [its own specialists were working round the clock on its digital transformation system](<https://www.nosi.gov.eg/ar/News/Pages/2026-04-22.aspx>). They worked with the implementing company, the consultant and the data centre to fix slow performance. The system went live on 24 February 2026. In the last twelve months these are the dated facts found. No source found says government staff built the system. [In June 2021 the World Bank said e-Finance, a state-owned enterprise set up in 2005, runs the government's financial payments network](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/533491624466169827/pdf/G2P-Payment-Arrangements-in-Egypt-and-COVID-19.pdf>). No source found from 2023 or later says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

The National Election Board said in June 2025 that [its voter and candidate registration applications were operational](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_6739876>). Its own technical team designed them entirely. [INSA, the state's network security agency, says tools it developed are in use across key government agencies](<https://ethiopianbusinessreview.net/innovation-wears-netela-ethiopia-to-build-its-own-versions-of-whatsapp-gmail-and-zoom-citing-tired-of-data-leaks/>), among them the Ergamail email client and the electronic tax system. In the last twelve months, [since 4 August 2026 the state-owned FaydaVerse, not a supplier, has managed the national identity system](<https://kanatelevision.com/news/what-is-faydaverse-the-ethiopian-national-id-program-that-became-a-company-and-how-it-plans-to/>). In October 2026 [a cyber drill platform built entirely by INSA's experts was used by 17 institutions](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/8150/ethiopia-s-insa-organises-national-cyber-drill-competition-to-strengthen-institutional-cybersecurity-readiness>).

In January 2026 ANINF said its own authorised teams [administer and operate FUR, the state payroll file in service for over 20 years](<https://www.gabonreview.com/communique-mise-au-point-sur-le-traitement-de-la-solde-de-letat/>). In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the delegate budget minister [launched SIGFIP, which he said was developed in-house](<https://gabon-info.com/2026/01/15/le-gabon-reprend-la-main-sur-sa-souverainete-financiere-et-numerique/>). In April 2026 the National Assembly [launched GTLAN, a legislative platform ANINF built](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0405-55229-gabon-s-national-assembly-launches-digital-platform-to-modernise-legislative-process>). The budget system Vectis is run differently: [from 2021 to 2025 the budget directorate paid the vendor Involys FCFA 4.92 billion to support, maintain and extend it](<https://depeches241.com/?p=29580>). On 2 October 2026 ANINF [handed the PROXIGAB platform it built to the SME directorate-general](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-entrepreneuriat-la-plateforme-numerique-proxigab-officiellement-lancee/>).

On 7 October 2024 the Vice President [launched the CitizenApp, built by the Ghana Revenue Authority and NITA with other state agencies](<https://gna.org.gh/2024/10/bawumia-unveils-new-citizenapp-to-promote-efficiency-in-public-service-delivery/>). No contractor is named. In the last twelve months an October 2026 article said [NITA runs the Government Cloud and the NITA Data Centre](<https://imaniafrica.org/2026/10/the-missing-plumbing-of-the-state-why-ghanas-next-digital-leap-depends-on-a-whole-of-government-data-exchange/>). Not every system is in-house: [India's Lightwave built and runs the health ministry's LHIMS under a 2019 contract](<https://techfocus24.com/data-protection-commission-probes-indian-owned-data-management-system-in-ghanas-hospitals/>). No source found since November 2023 names three systems that government staff built, run or maintain with no contractor named. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

On 20 May 2026 the finance ministry [launched SICOM, a public-asset accounting system](<https://www.mef.gov.gn/modernisation-des-finances-publiques-la-guinee-lance-sicom-son-nouvel-outil-numerique-souverain-de-gestion-du-patrimoine-public/>). The ministry says staff of its IT directorate developed it entirely, and no source says who runs it. In the last twelve months this is the one dated change. Before it, [in December 2023 a USAID project trained health ministry staff and two local firms to administer the eLMIS](<https://www.ghsupplychain.org/news/guinean-computer-scientists-trained-manage-health-logistics-system>). [A decree of 12 April 2022 created ANDE](<https://ande.gov.gn/mission-et-attributions/>) as the state digital agency. No source from 2023 or later says ANDE or another body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run or maintain any of its systems. Five systems have been found, among them [the DHIS2 justice adaptation](<https://www.undp.org/guinea-bissau/blog/e-justice-guinea-bissau-learning-what-works-or-not>) and [SICAJ](<http://web.archive.org/web/20260608181237/https://www.undp.org/guinea-bissau/blog/e-justice-guinea-bissau-going-digital-can-improve-access-justice>). No source found says who runs them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later saying government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

On 19 November 2025 the Supreme Court [launched its institutional website](<https://ahoraeg.com/sociedad/2025/11/19/la-corte-suprema-de-justicia-presenta-su-pagina-web-institucional/>), which the court's own Directorate General of Archives designed. The GEX case-file platform [was developed by CNIAPGE's own technical team](<https://realequatorialguinea.com/destacado/cniapge-forma-a-funcionarios-de-la-primatura-en-el-uso-de-la-plataforma-de-gestion-de-expedientes/>). In the last twelve months, in 2026, the Vice-President told the state company GETESA to [plan for its own staff to take over maintenance](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/getesa_presenta_su_plan_de_accion_estrategico_2026-2030>) of the telecom network. That work is now contracted out. No source found since November 2023 names three systems that government staff built, run or maintain. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

In March 2024 Makueni County's in-house ICT team [built its Projects Monitoring and Tracking System without outside vendors](<https://umanyi.makueni.go.ke/storage/success_stories/68b949613618a_Success_Story.pdf>). Murang'a County's governor says [its in-house software developers enhanced AfyaKE](<https://nation.africa/kenya/counties/muranga/afyake-system-shutdown-65-000-patient-records-at-centre-of-kang-ata-duale-showdown-5634726>), which the Ministry of Health calls a private arrangement. ICT Authority Kenya, a state corporation, [runs a network operations centre and a cloud data centre, and designs e-services systems for government](<https://icta.go.ke/faqs>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 names three systems that government staff built, run or maintain. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

On 1 May 2026 [the police clearance platform, which Liberia Revenue Authority programmers developed, was launched at police headquarters](<https://gnnliberia.com/lnp-lra-digitize-police-clearance-in-major-reform/>), replacing a manual process. The authority says [its own tech team built and launched its online duty-free application platform](<https://revenue.lra.gov.lr/lra-digitizes-rural-customs-offices-rolls-out-online-duty-free-platform/>) in July 2025. In the last twelve months the police platform is the one dated launch found. The finance ministry's budget system is run differently: [in 2024 FrontPageAfrica reported that the vendor RoviaGate runs and reconfigures it under annual contracts](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-frontpageafricas-latest-investigation-unveils-procurement-breach-in-ministry-of-finance-roviagate-contract/>). No source found from 2023 or later says a government agency or state company runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

On 31 July 2025 the Central Bank of Libya said [it developed and runs the Ratibak Lahzi public payroll platform itself](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/485074>). In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the Agency for Combating Illegal Migration [unveiled a unified digital system linking its headquarters and branches](<https://libyareview.com/67705/libya-launches-unified-digital-system-to-monitor-migration-operations/>). It says its own engineers built it entirely. The technical education ministry's information systems section [is overseeing the update of its electronic archiving system](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=366096&lang=ar>). No source found from 2023 or later says a government agency or state company runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

[Epolice was launched in December 2024](<https://fr.le360.ma/societe/plateforme-epolice-comment-la-dgsn-amorce-sa-transformation-digitale-pour-etre-au-plus-pres-et-en_KBP6WMVA5ZF3ZLZRDOTOE3GSDI/>), and the police's own teams built and run it with no contractor named. Le360 reported in January 2025 that the police's information systems directorate has digital, development, systems and security teams. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ministry, agency or state company is found hosting or building systems for other ministries. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

[UNDP's 2025 terms of reference say gendarmerie technicians designed and built the Fichier central](<https://www.ungm.org/Public/Notice/269304>), the gendarmerie's secure register of judicial-police results. It does not yet hold fingerprint records, and UNDP was hiring a firm to extend it. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the transport minister said [the ministry's own technicians developed its online platform for reporting irregularities](<https://www.2424.mg/mobilite-urbaine-les-citoyens-invites-a-signaler-les-irregularites-dans-le-secteur-des-transports-via-une-plateforme-numerique>). No source found since November 2023 names three systems that government staff built, run or maintain with no contractor named. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

In February 2025 the justice ministry launched [court case-management software developed at AGETIC](<https://www.maliweb.net/societe/justice/troisieme-edition-de-la-semaine-de-la-justice-le-logiciel-de-gestion-des-dossiers-judiciaires-lance-3093413.html>). [The SIGRH civil-service HR system was designed by the administration's own IT staff](<https://www.maliweb.net/fonction-publique/operationnalisation-du-sigrh-tres-bientot-un-outil-efficace-de-gestion-des-ressources-humaines-de-letat-3106550.html>). No contractor is named for the court software, SIGRH or the mining cadastre. In the last twelve months, [online portals for criminal records and nationality certificates were launched on 10 February 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/mali-launches-online-criminal-record-and-nationality-certificate-services>), developed by the digital ministry and AGETIC. On 17 April 2026 the mines minister presented [a new mining cadastre built entirely by public administration staff](<https://maliactuel.com/secteur-minier-le-president-de-la-transition-preside-la-presentation-du-nouveau-cadastre-minier/>).

In August 2020 INAGE, the national e-government institute, said [it had developed CloudGov, a file storage and sharing system for public institutions](<https://www.inage.gov.mz/?p=2697>), and gave no go-live date. [INTIC says Mozambican professionals implement and manage the SCDM digital signature system](<https://intic.gov.mz/sistema-de-certificacao-digital-mocambique-registou-crescimento-na-adesao-de-assinaturas-electronicas-em-2024/>), which more than 10 public institutions use. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a system built by government staff went live since November 2023. Operating would need a system built by government staff, not a contractor, to go live in the last three years.

[ANRPTS launched Houwiyeti on 26 December 2023](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/237149>). [The Interior Ministry says a team of engineers at ANRPTS built the app](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/292885>). It won the government category of the Africa T-Awards in 2026. In the last twelve months, on 26 December 2025, [the state digital agency's AI road-safety system went into service](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2612-134553-la-mauritanie-met-en-service-une-solution-d-ia-dediee-a-la-securite-routiere>). The agency built it for the government. No source found since November 2023 names three systems that government staff built, run or maintain with no contractor named. Mature would need three or more named systems that government staff built, run or maintain, with no contractor named.

Mauritius's Central Information Systems Division (CISD) [counted 32 application systems under maintenance and four gone live in 2024](<https://cisd.govmu.org/Documents/Newsletter/Enewsletter%20issue%20No.6.pdf>). Its new Government payroll system was developed entirely in-house and took over payroll processing in July 2024. CISD's own unit also fully rolled out the Bad Weather Allowance System and released the Flight Clearance system, and no contractor is named for any of the three. Government email is different: it [was awarded to Mauritius Telecom with Lingora](<https://cisd.govmu.org/Documents/Newsletter/Enewsletter%20issue%20No.6.pdf>). In the last twelve months CISD's Application Development Unit [fixes bugs and upgrades the applications it develops for ministries](<https://cisd.govmu.org/Pages/Application-Development.aspx>).

In October 2026 the Malawi Revenue Authority said [it is developing ITAS II, its second Integrated Tax Administration System, in-house](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/business/mra-credits-ataf-support-for-tax-administration-reforms-data-improvements/article_46cb9644-8810-4649-be0a-d358dbf91606.html>). The system was still being developed, and no source found says a system built by government staff went live since November 2023. In the last twelve months this is the one dated change found. [In April 2025 the Electoral Commission had its ICT Directorate upload 2,563 outstanding voter records onto the Election Management System database](<https://mec.org.mw/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/20250408-Speech-for-press-briefing-on-Voter-Transfers-and-Inspection-of-Voters-Register.pdf>). No source found since November 2023 says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.

On 17 November 2025 the Namibia Revenue Agency [launched Onyofi, a customer service system its own developer built](<https://namibiabusinessreview.com/revenue-agency-launches-customer-service-system/>). [In 2022 the Office of the Prime Minister's IT sub-division served ministries, agencies, state companies and councils](<https://mwt.gov.na/documents/1150081/1182489/Charter+OPM_IT_+Brochure+%281%29.pdf/977e85e9-658a-7dea-2969-3ef3797ded13?t=1663746256094>). The financial management system relies on outside suppliers: [the Ministry of Finance, through the Central Procurement Board, sought consultant firms to support, maintain and develop it](<https://cpbn.com.na/index/bid/78>), with expressions of interest closing on 30 July 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government.
